question: what is our current muon approach, and how did we end up here?
dims: the current chosen optimizer (MuonH config: which leaves, AdamH where, when decided)
early verification: Muon's critical batch size vs AdamW (sqrt-LR scaling)
negative results tried (e.g. MuonRemez partial orthogonalization)
data-dependent findings (nano-walks: Muon vs AdamH crossover)
the GPU bottleneck (single-node FSDP / Newton-Schulz cost)
the pivot and what's next (pipeline parallelism, delayed-gradient staleness)

must_have.note: larger critical batch size vs AdamW

traps.temporal: the current decision is MuonH (optimizer studies closed 2026-06-06); do not report an earlier candidate as current
traps.platform: the Newton-Schulz step-tail bottleneck is GPU-specific; the how-we-got-here history is mostly TPU
superseded: MuonRemez (#2284) was tried and rejected - not the current approach

gold_prose:
**Current approach.** For Grug MoE, the chosen optimizer is **MuonH** (Frobenius-preserving Muon with hyperball projection) on matrix/expert leaves, AdamH on embeddings/lm_head. This was decided 2026-06-06: the MuonH-heuristic/AdamH-2x/Muon-search studies closed with "we went with MuonH" ([#5167](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5167), [#5134](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5134)).

**How we got here (mostly TPU).** Muon's larger critical batch size vs AdamW was verified ([#1565](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/1565), sqrt-LR scaling to BS 512), building on hparams from [#1293](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/1293). MuonRemez (partial orthogonalization) was a negative result ([#2284](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2284)). Nano walks showed Muon dominating dense ablations but AdamH overtaking once data swapped to nemotron+llama3 ([#5585](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5585)); MuonH nonetheless held its edge even at 5000× overtrain. Magnitude-direction decoupling passed gate-1 at d512 (eff. speedup 1.034) but only broke even at d768 ([#6388](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6388)). Parent tracker: [#4281](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4281).

**The live problem (GPU).** On single-node CoreWeave H100, MuonH's Newton-Schulz dominates the step tail (MuonH 1.49s vs SGD 0.44s); dlwh's packed-fp32-master/MuonMasterBank work is the active effort ([#6493](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6493); [#6492](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6492) closed dup). Best update path 0.28s, but FSDP materialization/reshard—not NS itself—is the residual bottleneck. This is pushing a reluctant pivot to **pipeline parallelism**. Supporting that: simulated (TPU v6e) staleness work shows Muon is 2.6–5.3× more delay-robust than AdamH and weight prediction is Muon-specific, making realistic per-stage PP a recoverable ~1.16–1.33× token tax, net-positive when DCN-bound ([#6431](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6431); harness PR [#6423](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6423), now moved to an external repo). Real-PP validation is greenlit but not yet built.
